newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Police say little hope of survivors in ski lodges.
newsitem.headline: Police say little hope of survivors in ski lodges.

text.p: Australian police said on Friday there appeared little hope of finding survivors in the rubble of two ski lodges wrecked by a landslide on Wednesday.

"I think at this stage the chances are quite remote," Assistant Commissioner Ken Maroney told a news conference when asked about the chances that any of the 19 people in the rubble were still alive. Only one body has been recovered so far.
Police said heavy equipment would be put to work on Friday in the area where it was believed most of bodies were trapped.

They said conditions remained very dangerous for rescue workers and they were particularly concerned about bottles of liquefied petroleum gas and diesel fuel containers believed to be buried in the twisted ruins.
"It certainly poses a danger," the police commander said.

About 400 emergency workers are on the site, Australia's most popular ski resort about 400 km (250 miles) southwest of Sydney. The lodges were crushed by a landslide just before midnight on Wednesday.
